01 · How it works

From a DWG plan and ordinary photos to progress at each location.

01

Capture

Ordinary site photos from a phone, camera or drone, taken at coordinates from your plan. No special hardware.

02

Analyse

Each new photo is measured for pixel and colour change at its plan coordinate.

03

Compare

Progress is compared automatically with the DWG plan the contractor already has.

04

Act

Progress updates per coordinate, with email alerts on progress, stalls and deviations.

Illustrative concept with sample data. Working prototype; field test pending. Exploring next: camera GPS and LiDAR for higher precision.

02 · The prototype

Built on a real project's plan and imagery.

The prototype has been demonstrated on a real DWG file and real site photos. It has not yet run on a live site. The first field test is the next step.

Prototype interface, tested on a real project's plan and imagery. Field test next.

What it does today

  • Reads the DWG plan and builds a coordinate map of the site.
  • Measures pixel and colour change in site photos taken at plan coordinates.
  • Shows progress per coordinate.
  • Sends email alerts on progress, stalls and deviations.

What comes next

  • NextA field test on a live site, with a contractor or infrastructure owner.
  • ExploringCamera GPS combined with LiDAR, to place photos and measure depth more precisely.
  • PlannedIntegrations with the tools site teams already use.

03 · Who it is for

For the people who build and own the groundwork.

Groundwork and infrastructure contractors

You already have the DWG plan. WorkGuardAI uses it to show how far excavation and groundwork have come at each location, from photos your team can take on a normal site visit.

Public infrastructure owners

Cities and agencies that commission roads, utilities and public works can follow progress per location against the approved plan, measured from site photos.
